name: Question 14
problem:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $X∼N(0,{\sigma }^{2})$ is a normal random variable with $P(-3<X<3)=0.8472,$ use the table to find $\sigma ,$ rounded to $2$ decimal places.

| $z$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.04\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,1.3\,$ | $\,0.9066\,$ | $\,0.9082\,$ | $\,0.9099\,$ |
| $\,1.4\,$ | $\,0.9222\,$ | $\,0.9236\,$ | $\,0.9251\,$ |
| $\,1.5\,$ | $\,0.9357\,$ | $\,0.9370\,$ | $\,0.9382\,$ |

$\sigma ≈$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
First, we find the cumulative probability using symmetry:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-3<X<3) & =0.8472 \\ 2P(0<X<3) & =0.8472 \\ P(0<X<3) & =0.4236 \\ P(X<3)-P(X<0) & =0.4236 \\ P(X<3)-0.5 & =0.4236 \\ P(X<3) & =0.9236 \\ P(X\le 3) & =0.9236\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 3) & =0.9236 \\ P(Z\le \frac{3-0}{\sigma }) & =0.9236 \\ Φ(\frac{3}{\sigma }) & =0.9236 \\ \frac{3}{\sigma } & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.9236)\end{aligned}
$$

According to the table, we have

$$
Φ(1.43)=0.9236\,⇒\,{Φ}^{-1}(0.9236)=1.43.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{\sigma } & =1.43 \\ \sigma  & =\frac{3}{1.43} \\ \sigma  & ≈2.10\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $2$ decimal places.
